name: Nossis
bio: Nossis of Locri, in southern Italy, wrote epigrams around 300 BC. Her short poems often record dedications by women and portraits of women, and she is often linked with Sappho.
The epigrams here are the ones that Paton's first volume ascribes to her.

poems.title: Book V, 170
poems.author: Nossis
poems.text: “Nothing is sweeter than love; all delightful things are second to it, and even the honey I spat from my mouth.” Thus saith Nossis, but if there be one whom Cypris hath not kissed, she at least knows not what flowers roses are.

poems.title: Book VI, 132
poems.author: Nossis
poems.text: These their shields the Bruttians threw from their doomed shoulders, smitten by the swiftly-charging Locrians. Here they hang in the temple of the gods, praising them, the brave, and regretting not the clasp of the cowards they left.

poems.title: Book VI, 265
poems.author: Nossis
poems.text: Hera revered, who oft descending from heaven lookest on thy Lacinian shrine fragrant with frankincense, accept the linen garment which Theophilis, daughter of Cleocha, wove for thee with her noble daughter Nossis.

poems.title: Book VI, 273
poems.author: Nossis
poems.note: Paton heads this “Like Nossis” and lists it under Nossis with a query.
poems.text: Artemis, lady of Delos and lovely Ortygia, lay by thy stainless bow in the bosom of the Graces, wash thee clean in Inopus, and come to Locri to deliver Alcetis from the hard pangs of childbirth. ? A Lesbian Artemis, dedications to whom we possess.

poems.title: Book VI, 275
poems.author: Nossis
poems.text: With joy, methinks, Aphrodite will receive this offering from Symaetha, the caul that bound her hair ; for it is delicately wrought and hath a certain sweet smell of nectar, that nectar with which she, too, anoints lovely Adonis.

poems.title: Book VI, 353
poems.author: Nossis
poems.text: It is Melinna herself. See how her sweet face seems to look kindly at me. How truly the daughter resembles her mother in everything ! It is surely a lovely thing when children are like their parents.

poems.title: Book VI, 354
poems.author: Nossis
poems.text: Even from here this picture of Sabaethis is to be known by its beauty and majesty. Look at the wise house-wife. I hope to look soon from nigh on her gentle self. All hail, blessed among women !

poems.title: Book VII, 414
poems.author: Nossis
poems.text: Laugh frankly as thou passest by and speak a kind word over me. Iam the Syracusan Rintho, one of the lesser nightingales of the Muses; but from my tragic burlesques I plucked for myself a special wreath of ivy.

poems.title: Book VII, 718
poems.author: Nossis
poems.text: Stranger, if thou sailest to Mitylene, the city of lovely dances which kindled (?) Sappho, the flower of the Graces, say that the Locrian land bore one dear to the Muses and equal to her and that her name was Nossis. Go!

poems.title: Book IX, 332
poems.author: Nossis
poems.text: Let us go to the temple to sce the statue of Aphrodite, how cunningly wrought it is of gold. Polyarchis erected it, having gained much substance from the glory of her own body.

poems.title: Book IX, 604
poems.author: Nossis
poems.text: This is the picture of Thaumareta. Well did the painter render the bearing and the beauty of the gentle-eyed lady! Thy little house-dog would fawn upon thee if it saw thee here, thinking that it looked on the mistress of its home.

poems.title: Book IX, 605
poems.author: Nossis
poems.text: Callo had her portrait made exactly like herself, and hung the picture in the house of fair-haired Aphrodite. How gentle she looks standing there! Look how fresh is the bloom of her Cheri! All hail to her! for there is no fault in her life.

poems.title: Love's Sweetness (Mackail)
poems.author: Nossis
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Nothing is sweeter than love, and all delicious things are second to it; yes, even honey I spit out of my mouth. Thus saith Nossis; but he whom the Cyprian loves not, knows not what roses her flowers are.

poems.title: Rhintho (Mackail)
poems.author: Nossis
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: With a ringing laugh, and a friendly word over me do thou pass by; I am Rhintho of Syracuse, a small nightingale of the Muses; but from our tragical mirth we plucked an ivy of our own.

poems.title: Roses of Cypris
poems.author: Nossis
poems.text:
Of all the world's delightful things most sweet is love. The rest,
Ay, even honey in the mouth, are only second best.
This Nossis saith. And only they the Cyprian loves may know
The glory of the roses that in her garden grow.

poems.title: Rintho's Grave
poems.author: Nossis
poems.text:
Give me a hearty laugh, and say
A friendly word and go thy way.
Rintho was I of Syracuse,
A modest song bird of the muse,
Whose tears and smiles together sown
Have born an ivy all my own.
